text.p: A failure to regain the uptrend on Tuesday in the September notionnel contract on MATIF bodes ill for the recent bullish phase and increases the risk of a dip to 130.34, technical analysts said on Wednesday.
Feeble momentum means the contract will be penned in a narrow range with any move up likely grinding to a halt around resistance at 131.16, they added.
"On a break of 130.80, we could go to 131.16/30, some highs from last week...but that is rather questionable," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking.
"There's even less momentum in this market than in Bunds."
By 0750 GMT, the September notionnel was up 32 basis points at 130.92, after stalling briefly around 130.80 earlier.
Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said there was a risk the downside would gather momentum for a break to retest the 130.34 low from last Friday.
"Daily indicators have flattened a bit in neutral territory, but are still slightly negative," they said in a note.

"A break below the current minor uptrend support at 130.56 -- also potentially a head and shoulders top -- especially when confirmed with momentum to the downside, would signal retracement with an initial target at 130.06."
Deutsche said a resumption of the bullish trend would face stiff resistance near 131.06, an intraday retracement.
"For the bullish trend to be resumed, a gathering of momentum to break above 131.48 is required," they said.
"However, given the frail situation of the daily indicators, the weekly retracement at 131.78 still remains remote on this move."
By 0804 GMT, September Pibor was up 0.02 at 96.53.
